newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile will ease interest rates gradually - Massad.
newsitem.headline: Chile will ease interest rates gradually - Massad.

text.p: Chile will ease its year-long restrictive monetary policy gradually and investors should not interpret any cut in interest rates as the end of the credit squeeze, said Central Bank president Carlos Massad.
"It would be an error to interpret a future movement in Central Bank rates as the end of the adjustment," said Massad in a speech at a financial seminar.
"The change will occur gradually. When, will depend on economic variables."

The Central Bank has jacked up interest rates twice in the last year to cool Chile's robust economy, which was threatening to overheat and fuel inflationary pressure. The tightening in Chilean policy is known locally as "the adjustment."
The tightening has succeed in dampening economic expansion, with the latest data showing growth slowing to 5.5 percent in the third quarter from a galloping nine percent in the first quarter.

Despite the clear signs of a slowdown, Massad and Finance Minister Eduardo Aninat have said that rates will not be eased until the first half of next year until economic growth is firmly under control.
Any cut in rates will need to be gradual, or interest rates may have to rise again to prevent the economy veering from its low-inflation course, said Massad.

"A sharp or early easing of monetary policies could return us in the short term to even higher rates, if fears of rising inflation become rooted in people's expectations and (business) contracts," he said.
